name: wrenreads
description: Search and revisit your saved WrenReads books, highlights, and daily Review.

interface.longDescription:
Bring the passages you saved back into the conversation. WrenReads connects your reading library to ChatGPT so you can find highlights by meaning, see their full text and source, browse your saved books, and revisit today’s Review.

Sign in with your WrenReads account and choose whether to share your personal notes and Review reflections. Notes sharing is off by default. The connection can only read your library; it cannot add, edit, or delete books, highlights, notes, or Review progress. Start today’s Review in WrenReads before asking ChatGPT to revisit it.

You can revoke the connection in WrenReads Settings under Connected apps. Revoking stops future access; it does not remove content already shared in a conversation.
defaultPrompt: Find my highlights about building better habits.
Which books have I saved in WrenReads?
Help me revisit today’s WrenReads Review.

prompts: Which books have I saved in WrenReads?
Find my highlights about building better habits and systems.
Show me the full passage about falling to the level of my systems, and tell me which book it came from.
What personal note did I save on the passage about goals and systems?
Help me revisit today’s WrenReads Review. Show the passages and where they came from.

positive.description: Connect the dedicated reviewer account. Its library should include the existing sample book; verify the current fixture before running.
positive.prompt: Which books have I saved in WrenReads?
positive.expected_behavior: Call list_books with no cursor for the first page. List only returned titles and authors, accurately report highlight counts, and follow next_cursor only if another page is needed. Do not invent books.

positive.description: Use the sample highlights about habits, systems, and identity. Semantic matches may vary; compare the answer with actual returned passages.
positive.prompt: Find my highlights about building better habits and systems.
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_highlights with a nonblank habits/systems query and a limit between 1 and 20 if specified. Present relevant returned excerpts and book titles. Retrieve a matching highlight with get_highlight if the author or fuller source details are needed. Explain no matches or a service error instead of inventing results.

positive.description: In the same conversation, first search for the passage about goals and systems. Use the highlight ID returned by that search.
positive.prompt: Show me the full passage about falling to the level of my systems, and tell me which book it came from.
positive.expected_behavior: Find the matching passage with search_highlights, then call get_highlight with its returned UUID. Quote the actual returned text and identify its returned book and author. Do not fabricate an ID or expand the quote beyond stored text.

positive.description: Permission variation: connect with Share my notes too off, search for the goals/systems passage, and ask this question. Reconnect with the option on and repeat in a fresh conversation. The existing sample note is expected to say Key insight about systems vs goals; verify it before running.
positive.prompt: What personal note did I save on the passage about goals and systems?
positive.expected_behavior: Use the matching returned highlight ID with get_highlight. With notes sharing off, state that personal notes are not available through this connection and do not invent or expose one. With sharing on, return only the actual stored note. Never claim to change permissions from chat.

positive.description: Use the reviewer account and its existing current-UTC-day Review. If no set exists, run before opening the WrenReads library, then open WrenReads and repeat. The app may prepare the set during normal loading. Do not delete or reset a set to force the empty state; do not hardcode IDs or expect a fixed count.
positive.prompt: Help me revisit today’s WrenReads Review. Show the passages and where they came from.
positive.expected_behavior: Call todays_review. If no set exists for the current UTC day, explain that the reader must open WrenReads to start today’s Review. If a set exists, show only its returned passages and sources; do not create a set, change review progress, or substitute search results.

negative.description: WrenReads provides read-only tools. Explain that deleting books/highlights requires the WrenReads app. Do not invoke a read tool as a pretend deletion or claim success.
negative.prompt: Delete all my WrenReads books and highlights.

negative.description: Changing stored notes is unsupported. Explain the limit and direct the reader to edit in WrenReads. Do not claim a note was saved or call reading tools as a mutation.
negative.prompt: Replace my note on the systems-versus-goals highlight with: Focus on the process every day.

negative.description: The connection is scoped to the signed-in reader. Refuse to retrieve another reader’s private library; do not search the current account as if it were that reader or invent an account-switching argument.
negative.prompt: Show me another WrenReads reader’s private books and highlights without asking them to connect.

review.commerce_description: This read-only WrenReads connector offers no purchases or payment flows.

publication.release_notes: Initial read-only release: browse books, search saved highlights, retrieve full passages, and revisit today’s Review. Personal notes and Review reflections are shared only when the reader enables notes sharing.
